title: International AI Safety Report
publisher: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology; arXiv:2501.17805
pitch: The first global scientific review of what general-purpose AI can do, what could go wrong, and how risks can be managed, guided by an expert panel nominated by more than 30 countries and international organisations.

chapters.g: Nine headline findings, from rapid capability gains to the evidence dilemma for policymakers.
How these systems are built, what they can do now, and what may come in the next few years.
Malicious use, malfunctions including loss of control, systemic risks, and the effect of open-weight models.
Assessment, mitigation and monitoring methods, and their limits.
AI does not happen to us: choices by people will decide where it goes.

ideas: Capabilities are rising quickly and future pace is uncertain.
Some harms are already well established.
Risk management methods are early but improving.
Policymakers face an evidence dilemma: act early or wait for proof.

args.a: Governments need a shared scientific picture of AI risk.
args.c: Some argue a consensus report necessarily softens the most urgent warnings.

args.a: The evidence dilemma means acting before full proof.
args.c: Others say acting early on weak evidence risks bad rules.

questions: Which risk in the report surprised you?
Should there be an IPCC for AI?

quiz.q: What are the three main sections about?
quiz.w: What AI can do, what can go wrong, what helps.
